title: Our Lady, Undoer of Knots: The Augsburg Image and Devotion
summary: Our Lady, Undoer of Knots is not an apparition but a Marian devotion centered on a Baroque painting created in Augsburg, Germany, around 1700. The image highlights Mary's intercession in untying human difficulties and leading souls to Christ, remaining an approved private devotion.

blocks.text: 1. A Necessary Historical Clarification

The title 'Our Lady, Undoer of Knots' refers to a Catholic image and devotional tradition rather than a documented apparition with a visionary. Its center is a Baroque painting preserved in the Church of St. Peter am Perlach in Augsburg, Bavaria.

Painted around 1700 by Johann Georg Melchior Schmidtner, it was commissioned in connection with the Langenmantel family. Tradition links it to the reconciliation of a troubled marriage in 1615 after Fr. Jakob Rem prayed before an image of Mary.
2. The Augsburg Painting & Theological Root
The artwork depicts Mary standing between heaven and earth, carefully untying knots from a white ribbon handed to her by angels, while crushing the head of the serpent beneath her feet.

blocks.title: The Patristic Foundation (St. Irenaeus of Lyons)
blocks.text: “The knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience; what the virgin Eve bound through her unbelief, the Virgin Mary loosened by her faith.”
The knots symbolize sin, broken relationships, addiction, fear, and human entanglements. Mary’s action represents her maternal intercession, taking our tangled struggles to her Son.
I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; he shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.
Exegesis: The promise of victory over the serpent belongs decisively to Jesus Christ. Mary is associated with this victory through God's grace and her obedient consent to the Incarnation.
3. The Meaning of the Devotion

Calling Mary the 'Undoer of Knots' emphasizes her intercessory role. She does not replace Christ or independently control divine providence; rather, she brings our intentions before her Son and helps us cooperate with grace.

This devotion encourages believers to bring complex life challenges—such as family conflicts, anxiety, and addictions—to prayer, while actively taking responsible moral and practical steps toward resolution.

blocks.title: What the Image Teaches
blocks.text: Mary, Undoer of Knots, acts as an intercessor. She carries our tangled situations to Christ and assists us in acting with wisdom, truth, and grace.
4. Public vs. Private Revelation
Public Revelation was completed with the Apostles. The Augsburg image and its associated traditions are part of private devotion and do not add new dogmas to the Catholic faith.

blocks.title: CCC 67: Private Revelation
blocks.text: Private revelations do not belong to the deposit of faith. Their purpose is not to improve or complete Christ's revelation, but to help believers live it more fully in a specific time.
5. Church Recognition and Modern Spread

While there is no formal apparition inquiry, the image has enjoyed centuries of local ecclesial acceptance in Augsburg. Its global popularity surged after Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio (now Pope Francis) encountered it in Germany during the 1980s and promoted it in Argentina and worldwide.

blocks.title: Official Status
blocks.text: The image has long-standing local Catholic veneration and widespread papal encouragement. It is recognized as a pastorally fruitful Marian devotion rather than an apparition.
His mother said to the servants, 'Do whatever he tells you.'
Exegesis: At Cana, Mary's instruction remains clear: her intercession is never an end in itself, but a pathway pointing every soul toward obedience to Christ.
6. Pastoral Application
Praying to Our Lady, Undoer of Knots involves naming difficulties with honesty, surrendering them to Christ through Mary's prayers, and seeking sacramental grace in Reconciliation and the Eucharist.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: Our Lady, Undoer of Knots, invites us to place our tangled lives in God's hands, trusting that grace can untie every knot through faith, repentance, and charity.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer
blocks.text: O God of mercy, you gave us the Virgin Mary as a motherly sign of hope. Through her intercession, bring the tangled places of our lives before Jesus Christ, our Redeemer. Give us wisdom to recognize our sins, courage to seek help, and patience to accept your will. Mary, Undoer of Knots, pray for us and lead us always to Christ. Amen.
